subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: NEEDS_REVISION. Design correctly chooses real-history replay and fail-closed startup validation, but incorrectly treats patched() as occupying a fixed absolute command index. Core lookahead omits/skips patch calls absent from history, so inserting patched("B") above patched("A") does not alone invalidate history containing only A. Path B also overstates deprecatePatch: it is safe only after pre-patch histories are gone, while v2 is a separate subsequent versioning operation. Manifest design duplicates an existing dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json primitive; needed work is cryptographic file verification and atomic deploy/startup enforcement across every Worker.create path.

blockers.finding: Absolute patch-index premise is false: patched("B") inserted above recorded patched("A") is a supported lenient case when B is absent from history, so the proposed marker-only forward-drift fixture does not prove TMPRL1100.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Rewrite mechanism and test. Add a positive control proving absent B above A replays; make the negative control move A across an Activity, timer, or upsert command, or make A unreachable on the replayed path.

source.label: Temporal Core patch-marker handling
source.summary: Core skips nonmatching patch commands and fails only when a nondeprecated history marker has no corresponding patch command.

blockers.finding: Path B incorrectly presents deprecatePatch(oldId)+patched(v2) as a generic marker-relocation migration. deprecatePatch is safe only after no live pre-patch histories/workers remain; v2 is a distinct later patch.
blockers.in_scope_remediation: Split lifecycle into explicit phases. Prove every live target history contains oldId before replacing patched(oldId) with deprecatePatch(oldId); add patched(v2) only for a distinct subsequent command-changing branch with its own old/new replay fixtures.

blockers.in_scope_remediation: Extend existing bundle-manifest.json with a verifier that rehashes both files; validate source and copied payload; exclude manifest from rsync and publish last; centralize verification before every Worker.create path.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Caution. Design matches canonical Temporal approach: derive compatibility work from real replay histories, use patched/deprecatePatch only as versioned branches, and pin fixes with replay tests. It reuses existing local replay and manifest primitives rather than introducing a second subsystem. One design ambiguity remains: repository resolvers select workflows.ts solely when workflows.js is absent, so no existing explicit development/production boundary establishes when manifest enforcement may be bypassed. The verifier design must name a non-spoofable production discriminator and reject arbitrary workflowsPath overrides in production. Spec-law implication: extend existing replay-determinism and Worker.create drift guards, preserving no deletion/recreation, unchanged changeWorkflow signature, one manifest format, and real-history coverage.

validation.notes: No contract-breaking architectural conflict found. KD5 says development fallback is under an existing development-mode boundary, but current worker and in-process resolvers fall back by file existence alone. Before planning, define the exact production discriminator, permitted verified path(s), override policy, and tests for every production Worker.create route. Retaining workflowsPath is acceptable in this scope, with residual risk: Worker.create bundles its input at creation time; hash verification proves source-input identity, not compiled in-memory bundle identity.

tradeoffs: Captured production histories give strong compatibility proof but require payload-preserving sanitization and fixture review.
A shared verifier reduces drift but must cover single-queue, multi-queue, dynamic registration, and in-process creation routes.

Retaining workflowsPath minimizes scope but verifies input bytes rather than SDK-compiled workflow-bundle identity; prebuilt workflowBundle would strengthen identity but expands build/startup contract.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Temporal patching protects versioned branch selection; real command-producing operations still require replay-compatible order.
Temporal documents deprecatePatch only after pre-patch workers and histories are no longer live.
Existing manifest already hashes worker.js and workflows.js and is atomically published.
It can strengthen identity but changes build/startup contract beyond this agreement.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed after adding explicit production discriminator, allowed verified workflowsPath policy, and fail-closed test coverage for every production Worker.create route.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Proceed after adding one KD5 policy sentence and design-derived check: production is explicitly identified, accepts only canonical verified dist/temporal/workflows.js, rejects missing/mismatched manifest/artifacts as WORKER_BUNDLE_STALE before Worker.create, and permits workflows.ts only through an explicit development/test route. Extend static coverage to prove each production Worker.create route invokes the verifier first.

wisdom.content: Temporal patched() ordering model: wf.patched(id) does NOT occupy an immutable command index. sdk-core can SKIP a patch command absent from history — inserting patched("B") above existing patched("A") does NOT by itself fail replay of a history containing only A. TMPRL1100 "Non-deprecated patch marker ... no corresponding change command" fires when (a) a recorded nondeprecated marker has no REACHABLE patch command on the current path, or (b) actual command-producing operations (Activity/timer/UpsertWorkflowSearchAttributes) shift incompatibly AROUND the marker. Patch-to-patch ordering alone is not nondeterminism. Forward-drift regression must cross a real Activity/timer/upsert boundary, not merely insert/reorder patch calls. Source: github.com/temporalio/sdk-core workflow_machines.rs#L1737-L1794, patch_state_machine.rs; adv-researcher validation 2026-07-20.

Temporal deprecatePatch lifecycle: the SDK-blessed sequence is patched(oldId) → deprecatePatch(oldId) [after pre-patch executions are gone] → remove. deprecatePatch(oldId)+patched(newId-v2) is NOT a generic "relocate/change old branch" recipe — v2 is for a SEPARATE incompatible change. Deprecating oldId before all live pre-oldId histories are gone is unsafe. During replay, deprecatePatch(oldId) emits the matching internal patch command for histories that recorded it, without appending a fresh event. Source: docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/versioning; sdk-typescript internals.ts#L1198-L1212.

Advance worker-bundle manifest ALREADY EXISTS at dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json (generated by pnpm run build:worker), with reader at plugin/src/temporal/worker-bundle-manifest.ts. The freshness gap is NOT a missing manifest — it's that (a) the reader doesn't rehash workflows.js + worker.js against the manifest, (b) worker startup doesn't verify the manifest before Worker.create (workflowsPath loads during create, not run — verification must happen BEFORE create), (c) deploy-local.sh publishes the plugin manifest last/atomically but lets the worker manifest travel in the general rsync payload without equivalent hash verification. Also: the manifest hashes workflowsPath INPUT, but Worker.create compiles that path — doesn't prove final in-memory bundle identity; production guidance prefers prebuilt workflowBundle. Dev fallback loads workflows.ts when workflows.js absent — manifest enforcement must distinguish production from dev.

# Proposal: Fix Temporal patch nondeterminism

## Problem

Six ADV change workflows have produced TMPRL1100 replay failures, making workflow-backed reads and lifecycle operations unreliable. Current replay tests pass synthetic legacy histories but do not replay the affected production histories, so they cannot prove the deployed workflow code remains compatible.

## Confirmed evidence

- The affected histories report patch-marker or command-state-machine divergence.
- Patch-marker ordering alone is not sufficient proof of nondeterminism: Temporal can skip patch commands absent from a history. The exact failing command boundary must be established from each captured history.
- `dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json` already exists. The gap is runtime rehash/verification before `Worker.create`, production enforcement, and manifest-last deployment integrity—not manifest creation from scratch.
- `deprecatePatch` is lifecycle management after compatibility is established, not a generic way to relocate a patch branch.

## Direction

1. Export and sanitize each affected real history.
2. Reproduce and classify its exact replay divergence.
3. Apply the smallest evidence-backed deterministic compatibility fix; use Temporal patch lifecycle APIs only where their documented semantics apply.
4. Add replay regressions crossing real command-producing boundaries.
5. Reuse the existing worker-bundle manifest and verify artifact hashes before worker creation and during deployment.
6. Hand immutable histories to the recovery entry without deleting state.

## Scope

Temporal workflow determinism, replay fixtures, history classification, worker-bundle verification, deployment integrity, tests, and documentation. Recovery/retirement of immutable workflow state and disk-authoritative read architecture remain sibling Epic work.
documents.problemStatement:
## Problem

Multiple ADV change workflows are poisoned with Temporal replay nondeterminism (TMPRL1100), making them unqueryable and blocking reads/archive/cleanup project-wide.

Observed 2026-07-20 via adv_wip_state — poisoned workflows and their evidence:
- `fixArchiveDeltaReconciliation`, `fixScopeRepoFixture`, `makeLegacyDesignValidation`: "[TMPRL1100] Nondeterminism error: Non-deprecated patch marker encountered for change `acceptance-readiness-revision-v1`, but there is no corresponding change command! | QueryNotRegisteredError"
- `fixHealthViewTimeouts`: same, for patch `state-backed-acceptance-proof-v1`
- `refineTestEvidencePolicy`: "[TMPRL1100] Nondeterminism error: UpsertWorkflowSearchAttributesMachine does not handle HistoryEvent(id: 597, ActivityTaskScheduled) | QueryNotRegisteredError"
- `addArchiveScaleRegression`: query-wedged (RUNNING, historyLength 864)

## Known facts

- The patch markers ARE present in current source: `workflows.ts:1014` (`ACCEPTANCE_READINESS_FENCE_PATCH = "acceptance-readiness-revision-v1"`), `:1029` (`STATE_BACKED_ACCEPTANCE_PROOF_PATCH = "state-backed-acceptance-proof-v1"`), with `wf.patched(...)` calls at `:1085` and `:1088` and deprecatePatch guidance comments at `:994`/`:1026`. So this is NOT a naive "patch removed before histories closed."
- A replay-determinism regression harness exists (`src/temporal/__tests__/replay-determinism.test.ts` + recorded histories) but did not gate the deployed poisoning.
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts` is the worker-bundle root; the worker loads from `dist/temporal/` and requires `pnpm run build:worker`. Deployed-bundle staleness vs source is a leading hypothesis.

## Candidate root causes to disprove/confirm

1. Deployed worker bundle (`dist/temporal/workflows.js`) is stale / diverged from source, so replay runs code lacking the current patched() call sites while histories recorded the markers.
2. Patch-command ORDERING drift: a newer `patched()`/search-attribute upsert was inserted ahead of the recorded markers, shifting the deterministic command sequence (see the `UpsertWorkflowSearchAttributesMachine ... ActivityTaskScheduled` variant).
3. Histories were poisoned by a prior bad build and remain permanently non-replayable even under correct current code (→ recovery, not code-fix).

## Success (to be refined at agreement)

Exact trigger identified with evidence (which of 1/2/3, on which patch/event), a deterministic fix landed for any code-level cause, a replay regression that WOULD have caught it, and a clear handoff to the sibling "recover the 6 poisoned workflows" entry for any histories that cannot self-heal.

# Agreement: Fix Temporal patch nondeterminism

## Objectives

1. Establish the exact replay divergence for each of the six affected workflows from its real Temporal history rather than presuming patch-marker order is the cause.
2. Make the replay harness representative by adding sanitized production-history fixtures and command-boundary regressions.
3. Restore deterministic compatibility using the smallest evidence-backed change and the documented Temporal patch lifecycle where applicable.
4. Prevent stale or mismatched worker artifacts from reaching `Worker.create` by verifying the existing worker-bundle manifest and deployed artifacts.
5. Produce a typed recovery handoff for histories that cannot replay safely.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1 — Exact divergence classified

For each of `fixArchiveDeltaReconciliation`, `fixHealthViewTimeouts`, `fixScopeRepoFixture`, `makeLegacyDesignValidation`, `refineTestEvidencePolicy`, and `addArchiveScaleRegression`, evidence records the failing history event, current workflow operation, relevant introducing commit when identifiable, and one typed cause: `patch_branch_unreachable`, `activity_order_mismatch`, `timer_order_mismatch`, `search_attribute_order_mismatch`, `bundle_identity_mismatch`, or `unknown_with_evidence`.

### AC2 — Six real histories covered

At least six sanitized captured histories—one per affected workflow—are registered in the replay fixture corpus. Each fixture either reproduces the pre-fix failure and passes after remediation, or carries a typed `immutable_history` classification with a concrete replay error and recovery handoff. Sanitization review confirms proposal/agreement/task payload content is absent.

### AC3 — Evidence-backed compatibility fix

Every workflow-code change maps to an AC1 classification and a replay fixture. `patched`, `deprecatePatch`, or marker removal is used only according to Temporal's documented lifecycle and demonstrated history compatibility. No recorded marker is removed while a retained open history may require it, and no workflow entry signature changes.

### AC4 — Forward-drift regression

A deterministic regression moves or inserts a real command-producing workflow operation—Activity, timer, or search-attribute upsert—across a recorded history boundary and proves replay fails before the guard/fix. Patch-call reordering alone is not accepted as the failure oracle. CI reports the divergent fixture and operation.

### AC5 — Existing worker manifest enforced

`dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json` remains the canonical worker manifest. Production worker startup rehashes the declared worker/workflow artifacts and verifies the manifest before every `Worker.create` path. Missing or mismatched production artifacts fail closed with typed `WORKER_BUNDLE_STALE` evidence. Development source fallback remains explicit. Deployment verifies copied temporal artifacts and publishes their manifest last.

### AC6 — Recovery handoff complete

All six workflows end classified as `self_healed` or `immutable_history`. Each immutable classification records exact replay evidence and the target recovery Epic entry. This change does not delete or recreate workflow state.

## Success Criteria

- Six real-history fixtures registered and sanitized.
- Targeted replay suite passes every self-healed fixture and structurally validates every immutable classification.
- A command-boundary drift regression demonstrably fails against an incompatible worker variant.
- Every production `Worker.create` path is guarded by one shared manifest verifier.
- Build and deployment checks verify temporal artifacts and manifest-last publication.
- Full repository checks pass.

## Constraints

- No workflow-state deletion or recreation.
- No `changeWorkflow` signature change.
- No duplicate worker-manifest format or competing freshness subsystem.
- Captured fixtures contain no user-authored proposal, agreement, task, evidence, or secret payloads.
- Production startup fails closed; development fallback remains usable and explicit.
- Work runs in the ADV-managed change worktree.

## Avoidances

- Do not infer root cause from patch-marker position alone.
- Do not use `deprecatePatch` as a generic relocation mechanism.
- Do not remove markers without retained-history evidence.
- Do not create synthetic-only proof while real affected histories remain untested.
- Do not absorb disk-authoritative reads, archive durability, or workflow recovery into this change.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Auto-adopted/design-around: shared pre-`Worker.create` verifier, reuse of the replay fixture registry, command-boundary drift regression, and manifest-last temporal deployment. Production prebuilt `workflowBundle` remains an explicit design alternative requiring evidence against the installed SDK and is not silently adopted.

# Design: Fix Temporal patch nondeterminism

## Architecture Overview

The change uses one evidence pipeline with three enforcement layers:

1. **Capture and classify:** export each affected Temporal history, sanitize payloads, reproduce replay, and record a typed divergence classification.
2. **Remediate and regress:** select the smallest compatibility fix from the classification and pin it with the captured fixture plus a command-boundary drift test.
3. **Verify artifact identity:** reuse the existing temporal bundle manifest, verify hashes before every production `Worker.create`, and publish temporal artifacts before their manifest.

No marker strategy is selected before replay evidence exists. Immutable histories are classified for the sibling recovery entry rather than deleted or recreated.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — History evidence owns root cause

Each affected history produces a typed record containing workflow ID/change ID, failing event, current operation, introducing commit when identifiable, classification, replay result, and sanitized fixture reference. Allowed causes are the agreement's closed enum. No prose heuristic can authorize a workflow-code mutation.

### KD2 — Reuse the existing replay registry

Extend the current fixture registry and `Worker.runReplayHistory` harness. Add a sanitized history plus metadata for each affected workflow. Metadata validation rejects missing classifications, unsanitized payload indicators, duplicate workflow coverage, and immutable classifications without concrete replay evidence.

The capture path writes into a temporary location first. A deterministic sanitizer traverses payload-bearing history attributes, replaces user-authored payload bytes with replay-safe typed placeholders where possible, and emits a review summary. Fixture promotion requires an automated secret/content scan and explicit source review evidence.

### KD3 — Classification selects remediation

- `patch_branch_unreachable`: restore reachable branch structure or apply documented `patched → deprecatePatch → remove` lifecycle only when replay evidence proves compatibility.
- `activity_order_mismatch`, `timer_order_mismatch`, `search_attribute_order_mismatch`: restore deterministic operation order or add a compatible versioned branch around the real command boundary.
- `bundle_identity_mismatch`: correct build/deploy/startup identity enforcement; do not change workflow logic without replay evidence.
- `unknown_with_evidence`: no speculative mutation; classify immutable until a deterministic reproducer exists.

Every code change links to one classification and fixture. Patch-call reordering alone is never the failure oracle.

### KD4 — Command-boundary regression

Create a minimal test workflow/history pair where an Activity, timer, or search-attribute upsert moves across a recorded boundary. The incompatible worker variant must fail replay; the compatible variant must pass. Error output identifies fixture and operation. The test uses the official replay API and no production-only feature flags in workflow code.

### KD5 — Explicit artifact policy plus one shared pre-create verifier

Worker creation receives a required internal artifact policy:

```ts
type WorkerArtifactPolicy =
  | { mode: "production_verified"; manifestPath: string }
  | { mode: "development_source"; rationale: string }
```

Production entry points explicitly pass `production_verified`; tests and source-development entry points explicitly pass `development_source`. Mode is never inferred from manifest existence, environment guesswork, or a missing `.js` file.

Under `production_verified`, one pure verifier:

1. Resolves and schema-validates `dist/temporal/bundle-manifest.json`.
2. Resolves the canonical workflow artifact declared by the manifest.
3. Rejects a caller `workflowsPath` override unless it resolves to that declared artifact.
4. Rehashes every declared worker/workflow artifact.
5. Compares generation and hashes.
6. Returns a typed verified identity or `WORKER_BUNDLE_STALE` failure.
7. Runs before every production `Worker.create`, including single-queue, multi-queue, dynamically registered, and in-process production paths.

`development_source` permits the existing `workflows.ts` fallback only with an explicit rationale and never emits verified production identity. The verifier never silently regenerates manifests.

### KD6 — Manifest-last deployment

Mirror plugin-manifest publication semantics for temporal artifacts: exclude temporal manifest from bulk copy, copy artifacts, verify destination hashes, then copy manifest atomically last. A missing/malformed manifest or hash mismatch aborts deployment before worker restart.

### KD7 — Keep current `workflowsPath` model in scope

Production prebuilt `workflowBundle` could strengthen identity between verified bytes and SDK-consumed code, but it changes the build/startup contract and is not required to close the current stale-artifact gap. This change verifies the exact manifest-declared `workflowsPath` input before `Worker.create`. A prebuilt-bundle migration remains a separately evaluated alternative, not an implicit expansion.

## Interfaces and Data Shapes

```ts
type ReplayDivergenceCause =
  | "patch_branch_unreachable"
  | "activity_order_mismatch"
  | "timer_order_mismatch"
  | "search_attribute_order_mismatch"
  | "bundle_identity_mismatch"
  | "unknown_with_evidence"

type PoisonedHistoryClassification = {
  changeId: string
  workflowId: string
  fixture: string
  failingEventId: number
  observedError: string
  currentOperation: string
  introducingCommit?: string
  cause: ReplayDivergenceCause
  outcome: "self_healed" | "immutable_history"
  recoveryEvidence?: string
}

type WorkerBundleVerification =
  | { status: "verified"; generation: string; artifactHashes: Record<string, string> }
  | { status: "stale"; code: "WORKER_BUNDLE_STALE"; reason: string }
```

Schema validation, not free-form prose, owns fixture registration, artifact policy, and recovery handoff.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Add classification/sanitization schemas and capture support.
2. Export, sanitize, and register all six histories.
3. Record RED replay evidence and classifications before workflow edits.
4. Implement classification-specific compatibility fixes one cause at a time, rerunning the complete captured corpus after each change.
5. Add command-boundary forward-drift regression.
6. Add explicit artifact policy and shared verifier; cover every production `Worker.create` route structurally.
7. Add manifest-last deployment verification.
8. Run targeted replay/worker/deploy tests, smoke checks, full checks, and build verification.
9. Persist six terminal classifications for the recovery handoff.

## Affected Components

- Temporal replay fixtures, fixture metadata, and replay harness.
- History capture/sanitization support.
- Workflow code only where captured evidence requires compatibility changes.
- Existing temporal worker-bundle manifest reader/writer.
- Worker startup/registration paths.
- Deployment verification and tests.
- Determinism and deployment documentation.

## Design-Derived Criteria

1. Exactly six named affected workflows have fixture/classification coverage; duplicates or omissions fail validation.
2. Fixture promotion fails if bounded scans detect proposal, agreement, task, evidence, common secret formats, or unredacted payload codec data.
3. Every workflow-code diff carries at least one classification/fixture reference in test metadata.
4. The forward-drift regression crosses at least one real command-producing operation and fails against the incompatible variant.
5. Static coverage proves every production `Worker.create` route passes `production_verified` and invokes the shared verifier first.
6. Tests prove `workflowsPath` overrides fail closed under production policy and explicit development fallback remains usable.
7. Deployment publishes temporal manifest last and validates destination hashes before publication.
8. Full captured corpus replays after every compatibility change.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **History export unavailable:** record exact Temporal reachability/retention evidence; do not synthesize a substitute and claim real coverage.
- **Sanitization breaks replay:** preserve payload encoding/metadata shape, test sanitized replay before fixture promotion, and never commit raw histories.
- **Compatibility fix helps one history but breaks another:** run all captured fixtures after each mutation; one shared corpus is the merge gate.
- **Ambiguous production detection:** eliminated by required caller-supplied artifact policy; no ambient inference.
- **Manifest verifies input but not SDK-compiled output:** retain current contract for this change; evaluate prebuilt `workflowBundle` separately with installed-SDK evidence.
- **Overlap with later Hardening entries:** this change owns primitive verification and history evidence; sibling entries own state recovery, disk-authoritative reads, and broader release policy.

## LBP Analysis

This design removes speculative patch manipulation and makes every remediation traceable to executable history evidence. It reuses existing replay and manifest infrastructure, centralizes startup enforcement, makes production/development policy explicit, and keeps recovery boundaries intact.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Four adopted: shared pre-`Worker.create` verifier, existing replay-fixture registry reuse, command-boundary forward-drift regression, and temporal artifact verification with manifest-last publication. Production prebuilt `workflowBundle` remains a separately evaluated alternative.

## Independent Validation

Validator result: **caution**, medium risk. Temporal lifecycle and replay strategy were supported. Required correction: production/development detection and override policy must be explicit before planning. Resolved by KD5: required typed artifact policy, canonical manifest-declared `workflowsPath`, fail-closed production overrides, and structural coverage of every production `Worker.create` route.

## ADR Assessment

No new cross-project protocol or externally difficult-to-reverse contract requires an ADR. Artifact policy is internal and schema-checked.
